label: Baltimore City

county_election_office.name: Baltimore City Board of Elections, 417 E. Fayette St., Benton Office Building, Room 129, Baltimore 21202 (Baltimore City is a separate election jurisdiction from Baltimore County)

zip_caveats: ZIP 21201 (UMB campus, downtown west, Seton Hill and part of Mount Vernon): every 21201 polling place is in Congressional District 7, but the state legislative district splits block by block. Precincts that vote at the Steadman Fire Station (15 S. Eutaw St., next to UMB), Chase House (1037 Cathedral St.) and Samuel Coleridge-Taylor Elementary (507 W. Preston St.) are in Legislative District 40. Precincts that vote at the Central Pratt Library (400 Cathedral St.) and the Waxter Center (1000 Cathedral St.) are in District 46. So a 21201 voter gets either the District 40 or the District 46 Senate and House races, and Mount Vernon and downtown are split between the two. Look up your address to know which. Citywide: Congressional District 2 covers about 5% of city voters, in north Baltimore (polling places in 21209, 21210, 21211 and 21212); everyone else is in District 7. Legislative Districts 40, 41, 43A, 45 and 46 divide the city, and most city ZIPs touch two or more of them. ZIPs that cross into Baltimore County: 21206, 21207, 21209, 21212, 21215, 21222, 21224 and 21234 (21207, 21222 and 21234 are mostly county). 21225 crosses into Anne Arundel County. If you live on the county side of the line you get a Baltimore County or Anne Arundel ballot, not this one. These checks use polling-place locations from the state precinct list, not home addresses, so treat them as a guide. Students at UMB and other city schools: Maryland lets you register at your school address or your home address, but only one. Before reading this ballot, check where you are registered with Maryland's voter lookup (voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/VoterSearch; it shows your precinct and polling place). Registered somewhere else? This ballot doesn't apply; use that place's mail ballot. Not registered at your Baltimore address yet? You can register and vote in one trip at any Baltimore City early voting center, Oct 22 to 29, 7 AM to 8 PM, with proof of your Baltimore address. The closest to UMB is the University of Maryland Engagement Center, 16 S. Poppleton St.
notes: On November 3, vote at your assigned polling place, 7 AM to 8 PM. Use the Maryland polling-place lookup to confirm it; the city has published its final 2026 general-election list. Early voting is October 22 to 29, 7 AM to 8 PM, at any Baltimore City early voting center. The state general-election drop-box list, updated August 26, includes the University of Maryland Engagement Center, 16 S. Poppleton St. Return a mail ballot by 8 PM on November 3 to an official drop box, an early voting center (through Oct 29), your polling place on Nov 3, or the local board. Baltimore City and Baltimore County are separate election jurisdictions.
